races.title: State House, District 14
races.note: Unopposed: this seat was decided without a general-election contest, so it won't be on your ballot.

cands.name: Kimberly Daniels
cands.bio: Democratic state representative for House District 14 (part of Duval County). Minister and author; former Jacksonville City Council member (elected 2011); in the House 2016-2020 and again since 2022. Unopposed in 2026.
cands.local_ties: Jacksonville, Duval County (per Wikipedia and district).

record.text: Sponsored HB 839 (2018) requiring public schools to display the motto "In God We Trust"; it passed the House 97-10 and was later adopted as law in 2019 as part of an education bill. Sponsored 2019 legislation to require Bible-teaching courses in schools (approved by a House subcommittee).
Lost the 2020 Democratic primary to Angie Nixon; won the seat back in 2022 and was re-elected in 2024.

controversies.text: 2017: Florida Elections Commission found probable cause she used campaign funds for personal expenses; she agreed to pay a $1,500 fine for the 2015 complaint.
2019: she admitted filing inaccurate financial disclosures for 2012-2014.

2019: she championed a $1 million state contract for SCLC World Wide; the Department of Juvenile Justice later sued the organization for not delivering, and a former staffer sued her claiming wrongful firing (outcomes not found).

cands.gaps: Recent endorsements, donors and links not found (search budget exhausted); Wikipedia text is the only source and the controversies are from 2015-2019. Owner-source search (Stew Peters, Alex Jones, Owen Shroyer) was NOT run: the shared web-search budget was exhausted before this candidate was reached, so absence of hits means nothing.

votes.what: Joint resolution putting Amendment 3 (Save Our Homes property-tax changes: higher homestead exemption, lower assessment-increase limits) on the Nov 2026 ballot.
The 2025-26 General Appropriations Act (state budget), final vote.
Immigration enforcement bill from the 2025 special session: state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Post-hurricane emergency management bill that also limits local governments' ability to adopt stricter development rules after storms.
Online Protections for Minors: restricts social media accounts for minors.
Interests of foreign countries: restricts land purchases near military sites and critical infrastructure by people from China and other 'countries of concern'.
Education: expands school voucher eligibility to all Florida K-12 students.
Heartbeat Protection Act: bans most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy.
Public Safety: lets most adults carry a concealed firearm without a permit (permitless carry).
Property Insurance: creates the Florida Optional Reinsurance Assistance program (FORA) for insurers.
